- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., post-0.37 sentiment spikes, model overshoots).
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.70 or -0.63), model tends to lag or underestimate drop.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecasted mean by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior 30d average.
- If model shows upward trend after a recent dip, check sentiment for reversal — if sentiment is still negative, cap forecast at prior 7-day high.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >2% in 3 consecutive days, adjust next forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.03), model tends to overreact — reduce forecast by 0.3–0.8% to align with mean reversion bias.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often overestimates — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% to forecast.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is consistently 0.5–1.0% below model, reduce forecast by 0.2–0.5% for next period to avoid mean reversion miss.
